notes:
Overview:
- GlidePath builds low-latency personalization and re-ranking for web + mobile ad placements and in-app recommendations. Strong realtime SLAs for user-facing flows.

Key requirements (from CTO / infra lead):
- Workloads: live chat for A/B test assistants, 1: many personalizations per page (reranking), embeddings for similarity/feature store.
- Latency targets: p50 <= 8ms, p95 <= 28ms for rerank single-request path; chat interactive p95 <= 120ms (but aiming for <80ms with caching).
- Throughput: baseline 2k reqs/s, peak bursts to 6k reqs/s during campaign launches.
- Cost sensitivity: high — want predictable unit economics. Interested in reserved capacity but need evidence of 35-50% token-cost reduction with batching/caching/quant.
- Model preferences: open-models preferred (Llama-2-family / Mistral variants) with 4-bit or int8 quantization as acceptable trade-off if quality holds.
- Routing/fallback: multi-tier routing (low-cost quantized variant for bulk rerank, high-quality for top-1 scoring); geo fallback to EU/NA.
- Security/regulatory: EU data residency, SOC2 compliance, SSO (SAML/Okta), KMS control for keys, audit logs retained 12 months, retention controls for PII.

POC & perf notes (SE run):
- 2026-01-12 discovery call (Priya). Agreed to 3-stage perf POC.
- 2026-02-10 initial bench: baseline unoptimized 13B model on public cloud -> p95 ~ 120ms for single rerank, p95 ~ 360ms for chat (cold).
- 2026-02-18 warm-KV-cache run: prefix caching reduced median tokens by ~38% for chat demos; p95 improved to ~85ms.
- 2026-02-26 quantization test: 4-bit quant reduced CPU/GPU time by ~2.8x, rerank p95 observed ~42ms but noticed occasional semantic drift on long-tail prompts.
- Current ask: Redwood to run high-concurrency benchmark (2k->6k rps) with continuous batching and adaptive cache eviction; include trial of scheduling policy that prioritizes low-latency tails.

- "If we can hit 25-30ms p95 on rerank at scale, reserved capacity makes sense" — CTO (S. Müller).
- Product lead: wants detailed breakdown by token + per-request latency for canary vs baseline.
